props.title: Gomorrah
props.initialSlug: Raw portrait of Naples' brutal crime underworld

sections.content: **Gomorrah** (2008) revolutionized mafia cinema by stripping away all glamour from organized crime. Unlike the operatic scope of **The Godfather** (1972) or the seductive energy of **Goodfellas** (1990), director Matteo Garrone presents a brutal, documentary-style examination of Naples' Camorra crime syndicate. The film interweaves five stories showing how the mafia infects every level of society - from teenage drug runners to toxic waste disposal. Its unflinching realism earned comparisons to **City of God** (2002) for showing criminal empires through a raw, localized lens.

sections.content: Garrone's influence rippled through Italian crime cinema, inspiring a new wave of neo-neorealist mafia narratives. **A Ciambra** (2017) follows a 14-year-old Romani boy drawn into crime in Calabria, while **Dogman** (2018) examines how small business owners get crushed between rival criminal factions. These films share Gomorrah's commitment to depicting crime's systemic nature rather than individual anti-heroes.

The success of Gomorrah also sparked renewed interest in exposing specific regional mafias. **Black Souls** (2014) delves into the 'Ndrangheta of Calabria, while **The Traitor** (2019) dramatizes real Cosa Nostra informant Tommaso Buscetta's testimony. These films continue Gomorrah's mission of demystifying organized crime through granular, region-specific storytelling. SUBHEAD: Impact on International Crime Cinema

sections.content: Gomorrah's influence extends beyond Italy. **Animal Kingdom** (2010) brought similar documentary-style realism to Australian crime families, while **A Prophet** (2009) examined French prison gangs with comparable sociological depth. The HBO series **The Wire** (2002-2008) shares Gomorrah's systematic approach to criminal ecosystems, though it preceded the film. These works collectively shifted crime narratives away from personality-driven stories toward examinations of criminal infrastructure.
